# Installation of R and RStudio {#sec-setup}

## R and RStudio

1. Install **R** (version 4.4 or later) from <https://cran.r-project.org>, selecting the appropriate operating system (for Windows: *Download R for Windows → base*).
2. Install **RStudio Desktop** (free of charge) from <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>.
3. Open RStudio. R runs within RStudio and does not need to be opened separately.

Where software cannot be installed locally, **Posit Cloud** (<https://posit.cloud>) can be used in a web browser.

## Packages

The following code installs all packages used in the course. Installation requires an internet connection and takes approximately 5–15 minutes.

```{r}
#| eval: false
packages <- c(
  "tidyverse",     # data management and visualisation
  "deSolve",       # differential equations (compartmental models)
  "outbreaks",     # historical outbreak datasets
  "fitdistrplus",  # fitting of delay distributions
  "EpiEstim",      # time-varying reproduction number
  "epichains",     # branching processes
  "finalsize",     # final size in age-structured populations
  "socialmixr",    # social contact matrices
  "coda",          # MCMC diagnostics
  "patchwork",     # combination of figures
  "knitr", "rmarkdown"
)
install.packages(setdiff(packages, rownames(installed.packages())))
```

The installation can be verified with a small SIR model:

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(deSolve)
out <- ode(y = c(S = 999, I = 1, R = 0), times = 0:50,
           func = function(t, y, p) with(as.list(c(y, p)), {
             list(c(-b * S * I / 1000, b * S * I / 1000 - g * I, g * I))
           }),
           parms = c(b = 0.5, g = 0.25))
plot(out)
```

The installation is successful if three plots (S, I and R against time) are displayed.

## Course materials

The materials of the course itself are available at <https://github.com/Federica-Giardina/TIMERA> (*Code → Download ZIP*). After unzipping, the folder should be opened as an RStudio Project (*File → New Project → Existing Directory*).

## Datasets

All datasets used in Module 1 can be downloaded as CSV files in a single archive, [TIMERA-datasets.zip](https://federica-giardina.github.io/TIMERA-preparatory/datasets/TIMERA-datasets.zip), which also contains a description of each dataset and its source. The CSV files can be opened in R, Excel or any statistical software.
